title: Fourteen Autumns and One Short Door
subtitle: 安全预防 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 安全预防（灾害防范·安全与预防）
meta: 主题语境：安全预防（灾害防范·安全与预防）　|　核心词汇：elevator　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 elevator 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 my father ① took an elevator that no worker in the building would have trusted, and he said the taking was the whole of the autumn. The ② elevator, meaning the lift and not the hoist, ran fourteen autumns and stayed unnamed in the book; an elevator, he said, is the only thing in a building that is judged by how long it is left untrusted.

Every ③ elevator in that building had the same short door at the end of it, and the ④ elevator at the end, meaning the one they kept for the goods and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An elevator, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to trust; my father said the trusting is the part that fills fourteen autumns.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the elevator was the whole of the story, meaning the hoist and not the lift. The ⑥ elevator, meaning the hoist and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody relies on and nobody inspects; elevator, he said, is either something you take or the only word that means both a lift and a hoist. He said the hoist is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ elevator had become a line in a checklist, and the checklist had become an argument about the short door. The ⑧ elevator of the whole thing, my father wrote in October, was one building and fourteen autumns of trusting; elevator, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to trust. She said the trusting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ elevator I remember is the one named in the checklist, which stopped in 1982 and is still described as the quietest in the building. An ⑩ elevator, my mother said in 1984, is the only one that improves by being trusted; every elevator, she said, is a hoist that has agreed to look like a lift. She said the hoist was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 电梯（指那座楼里乘过的那一部）
B. n. 电梯（指那部电梯本身，与升降机相对）
C. 固定搭配：take an elevator 乘一部电梯
D. n. 电梯（指留给运货的那一部）
E. n. 电梯（抽象总称，指一座楼的乘梯之事）
F. n. 电梯（指巡检表上写到、被列名的那一部）
G. n. 升降机；提升装置（指故事里人人都靠它却无人检查的那样东西）
H. n. 升降机（抽象总称，指人人都靠它却无人检查的那种装置）

items.q: took an elevator that no worker in the building would have trusted
The elevator, meaning the lift and not the hoist
the elevator was the whole of the story
the elevator had become a line in a checklist
The elevator of the whole thing
An elevator, my mother said in 1984

answers.why: take an elevator 意为“乘一部电梯”，1961 年父亲乘了一部楼里没有一位工人肯信任的电梯。
elevator 意为“电梯”，指那部电梯本身而不是升降机，它经过了十四个秋天而在簿子上没有名字。
elevator 意为“电梯”，指那座楼里的每一部电梯，每一部到头都有同一道短短的门。
elevator 意为“电梯”，指留给运货的那一部，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
elevator 意为“升降机、提升装置”，指故事里人人都靠它却无人检查的那样东西，叔叔说这台升降机就是那个故事的全部。
elevator 意为“升降机”，指人人都靠它却无人检查的那种装置而不是那部电梯，是故事里人人都靠它、却无人检查的东西。
elevator 意为“电梯”，指巡检表上写到、被列名的那一部，到 1970 年这部电梯成了巡检表里的一行。
elevator 意为“电梯”，父亲十月写道，整件事的乘梯之事是一座楼和十四个秋天的信任。
elevator 意为“电梯”，我记得的是巡检表上列名的那一部，1982 年停了，至今仍被说成楼里最安静的一部。
elevator 为抽象总称，母亲 1984 年说，一部电梯是唯一会因为被好好信任而变得更好的东西。
